milestones.title: M0 · Foundations
milestones.description: A buildable app skeleton with CI, the Clipra theme, and the three risky technical bets (layered compositing, whisper.cpp, export speed) proven on real devices.

milestones.title: M1 · Projects and timeline
milestones.description: Create a project in any format, import media, arrange it on generic layers, preview it on proxies and edit it with split, trim, move, undo and redo.

milestones.title: M2 · Compositing
milestones.description: Clips on higher layers can be moved, scaled, rotated, blended with 16 modes, keyframed, sped up or slowed down, and graded by adjustment clips.

milestones.title: M3 · Effects
milestones.description: All 24 filters (Mosaic included), 24 transitions, rectangle and oval masks, and color grading with LUTs work in preview and export.

milestones.title: M4 · Text
milestones.description: Text cards and titles with 12 effects, animations and templates.

milestones.title: M5 · Audio
milestones.description: Per-clip volume, fades and loudness, noise reduction, on-device AI voice cleanup, ducking, beat markers and voiceover recording.

milestones.title: M6 · Captions and edit by text
milestones.description: Whisper captions on the device with styles, editing, .srt and offline translation, plus editing the video by deleting words and pauses.

milestones.title: M7 · Vision tools
milestones.description: Person cutout, chroma key, face-following masks, auto-reframe and video stabilization, all on the device.

milestones.title: M8 · Export
milestones.description: Export in HD to 4K with H.264, HEVC or AV1 from original media, in the background, with extras (.srt, .jpg, .m4a, .otio) and a Saved screen.

milestones.title: M9 · Ads and Clipra Pro
milestones.description: Two compliant interstitial ads per export for free users, consent where required, and a 10 PLN one-time Clipra Pro purchase that removes them.

milestones.title: M10 · Tablet
milestones.description: A landscape three-pane tablet experience for every feature.

milestones.title: M11 · Launch
milestones.description: Onboarding, settings, accessibility, Polish and English, performance on real devices, and a Google Play release.

issues.title: Foundations: skeleton, CI, theme and technical spikes
issues.goal: Set up the Android project so every later milestone can start in parallel, and remove the biggest technical unknowns early. The spikes decide whether Media3 can do layered compositing with custom blend modes and transitions, how fast whisper.cpp is on real phones, and how fast 1080p export is. Their results update `docs/architecture.md` before M1 starts.
scope: Gradle multi-module project as in the architecture doc
CI on GitHub Actions
Compose theme and shared components from `design/tokens.json`
Spikes: layered compositing, whisper.cpp, export performance
Dependency license policy and third-party list
acceptance: `./gradlew build` passes on CI for every pull request
The app launches to a themed Home placeholder on a phone and a tablet emulator
Spike reports are committed under `docs/spikes/` and architecture decisions are updated
No dependency outside the license policy
notes: If Media3 cannot blend layers with custom modes, plan a custom GL compositor (adds about two weeks to M2)
If whisper base is too slow on mid-range phones, default to tiny and offer base as an option

scope: Gradle version catalog, Kotlin 2.x, Compose, Hilt, kotlinx.serialization, Room, DataStore, WorkManager
Modules: app, core:designsystem, core:model, core:data, core:engine, core:audio, ml:whisper, ml:voice, ml:vision, ml:translate, feature:* (empty), monetization
minSdk 26 (proposed), latest targetSdk required by Play, arm64-v8a first

Navigation shell with placeholder destinations for every board in `design/README.md`
acceptance: Project builds and installs on a device
Each module compiles independently and has one example unit test
Navigation reaches a placeholder for every phone board
notes: Keep feature modules independent of each other; share through core modules

issues.title: Spike: layered compositing, blend modes and transitions on Media3
issues.goal: Prove that Media3 (Transformer and CompositionPlayer) can render the Clipra layer model, or decide on a custom GL compositor.
scope: Build a composition with 3 overlapping video layers, one photo and one text overlay, with gaps between clips on a layer
Implement Screen and Multiply blend modes as custom shaders
Implement one transition (Dissolve) across a cut
Preview with CompositionPlayer and export 1080p30 with Transformer
Measure preview frame rate and export time on a mid-range and a low-end phone
acceptance: Written report in `docs/spikes/engine.md` with numbers, code sample and decision
Decision on layer ordering, gaps, compositor and transitions recorded in `docs/architecture.md`
notes: Media3 docs state that cross-fading video is not supported yet; transitions likely need a custom effect

issues.title: Spike: whisper.cpp on Android with word timestamps
issues.goal: Know how fast and accurate on-device captions are before building the captions feature.
scope: Build whisper.cpp for arm64-v8a with JNI
Transcribe a 42 s English and a 42 s Polish clip with tiny, base and small models
Get word-level timestamps and confidence
Measure time, memory and battery on two devices
acceptance: Report in `docs/spikes/whisper.md` with real-time factors and word error impressions
Recommendation for the default model and chunking strategy
notes: Model sizes (official files, decimal MB): tiny 78, base 148, small 488, large-v3-turbo q5_0 574

notes: Logic reference: `design/canvas/NewProject.dc.html` renderVals()

Resolution p is the short side in every ratio: landscape H = p and W = p × w / h, portrait W = p and H = p × h / w, the computed side rounded to the nearest even number; square p × p (16:9 4K = 3840 × 2160, 21:9 FHD = 2520 × 1080)

issues.title: Video stabilization
issues.goal: Smooth out handheld shake in a clip on the device, cropping as little as possible.
scope: Motion analysis on the device: track corners between frames of the proxy at reduced size (Shi-Tomasi corners, pyramidal Lucas-Kanade) and estimate each frame's camera motion with RANSAC (shift, rotation, scale), so moving subjects don't count
Smooth the camera path and move each frame onto it, with one zoom for the whole clip, just large enough that no edge shows
Strength 0 to 100 (default 50) trades smoothness against crop; the crop is shown
Background analysis (WorkManager) with progress and cancel, cached per media hash; the clip plays unstabilized until it is ready
Rendering through a per-frame matrix effect in the clip's Media3 effect chain, the same in preview and export
`stabilize` setting on the clip in the project model; Stabilize in the phone clip tools and the tablet toolbar
acceptance: Handheld test clips (walk, slow pan, static shot with a person walking through) come out clearly steadier, and intended pans are kept
No black edges at any strength
Analysis of a 42 s 1080p clip takes under 15 s on a mid-range phone (to confirm)
Export matches preview
Unit tests: a still image moved along a known shake path is recovered within 1 px at proxy size; the zoom always covers the frame
OpenCV adds under 5 MB to the arm64 download (to confirm)
notes: Classical method, no model: the standard way editors stabilize imported clips, with nothing to download, and it runs on any phone. Not used: gyro data (most phone videos carry none, and Gyroflow is GPL-3.0) and learned stabilizers (StabNet, DUT, NNDVS are research code without official mobile builds). Revisit a model only if one ships with a permissive license and an official on-device version
OpenCV (Apache-2.0) for corners, optical flow and RANSAC: build only core, imgproc, video and calib3d (with what they need) for arm64-v8a; the full official package is far too large
Store the path in normalized units keyed by timestamp (phone video is often variable frame rate), so it fits the proxy and the original and survives trims, speed changes and reverse

Cutout masks and face tracks are computed on source frames, so they go through the same transform; the user's transform, crop and masks apply after it. Share path smoothing with face follow and reframe
No board for the Stabilize sheet yet: build it from the design system like the other clip tool sheets
Not in v1: rolling-shutter (wobble) correction and full-frame stabilization without crop
